articles.title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Grades, analysis and details from every key deal
articles.summary: We'll be tracking and grading the trades across the NFL up until the Nov. 10 deadline.
articles.body:
The NFL trade market is open with several high-profile deals already done. We'll be tracking and grading the trades across the NFL up until the Nov. 10 deadline.

Colts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

The Colts have other players who are far less tethered to the organization who also soon could be moved. Lacking a first-round draft pick next year from the Sauce Gardner trade, the Colts are trying to recoup as much draft-pick value as possible before the spring. With Daniel Jones' struggles, along with the Colts' apparent lack of trust in Anthony Richardson Sr., the team almost certainly will be going QB hunting in the offseason. …

Given the stage of his career and his contract status, this could end up being a fairly pricy rental for the Seahawks — and that potential cost must be baked into the team's grade. But if Nelson plays to his expected level, or even above the level he's played at this season, and the Seahawks remain a title contender, it would be hard to label this as anything but a win. – Eric Edholm

The 49ers needed defensive help up front, and Buckner looks like the right-shaped peg for their hole inside. Osa Odighizuwa has supplied some pressure, and rookie Gracen Halton has had some big moments, but they're the only Niners DTs to play every game. There weren't many other dependable pieces inside. It was also a group that lacked length and the ability to close down passing lanes. Odighizuwa and Halton have the only two batted passes for the team this season. …

The Colts got about what could be expected in return, and considering how depleted their draft-pick drawer is with no first-round pick next year, every pick counts. Even with the 2027 selections they got for Nelson and Buckner likely falling closer to the ends of those respective rounds, the Colts are accumulating more immediate assets to compete for a quarterback next year. It's smarter than waiting a year for compensatory-pick value, even if they're having to pay for past sins. – Eric Edholm

Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 sixth-round pick

Cardinals receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick

Nobody outbid the Houston Texans for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Whether that's a win for the Texans remains to be seen.

The Texans landed Harrison, the disappointing receiver from the Arizona Cardinals. It was reported Oct. 10 that the Cardinals were finalizing details on a trade for Harrison, but no team was announced. No team made a better offer to the Cardinals at the last minute, so Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick go to Houston for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

It gives Harrison a second chance. And Arizona recoups some value after a draft whiff on Harrison. – Frank Schwab

Ravens receive: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles receive: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

The timing, one day after longtime Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly announced his retirement , is perhaps the most surprising element of the trade.

The Ravens, who have had a hard time replacing Tyler Linderbaum at center, recently watched as Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic all suffered injuries, forcing 2026 first-rounder Vega Ioane over from guard to center.

Jurgens now figures to be Baltimore's center for multiple seasons, given the nature of his contract after he signed an extension last year. – Eric Edholm

Steelers receive: 2027 seventh-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Jerry Jones said before the season that he was itching to make another big trade .

The Dallas Cowboys owner made a move, with room to possibly make another splash before the deadline. Dallas dealt a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for their young cornerback Joey Porter Jr., a second-round selection in 2023.

It wasn't the all-in move Jones has teased. But it's still a big move that should help improve a defense that hasn't been great to start the 2026 season . – Frank Schwab

Is J.J. McCarthy, who fell from first- to third-string quarterback quickly in Minnesota, the answer for a Giants team that lost not only Jaxson Dart but also its top pass rusher in All-Pro Brian Burns (season-ending ACL tear) ? How quickly can McCarthy acclimate to a new offense, new terminology and new cast of supporting teammates?

McCarthy played and started 10 games in two-plus seasons as a Viking, winning an impressive six. But that record often reflected the talent around him and even moreso, the strength of the Vikings' defense.

McCarthy threw 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in his 10 Vikings games. Since he was drafted in 2024, his 72.6 passer rating ranks 43rd out of 44 quarterbacks who have started at least 10 games. Only Anthony Richardson Sr., whom the Indianapolis Colts tried and failed to trade in the spring, has posted a lower mark. — Frank Schwab (grades) and Jori Epstein

Cowboys receive: OL Broderick Jones, 2027 fourth-round pick

Steelers receive: 2027 3rd-round pick, 2027 seventh-round pick

There was excitement for the Pittsburgh Steelers when they drafted Georgia offensive tackle Broderick Jones with the 14th overall NFL Draft pick in 2023. They even traded up to take him.

The excitement ran out when the Steelers traded Jones to the Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys sent a third- and sixth-round pick to the Steelers for Jones and a fourth-round pick.

Jones had dealt with a neck injury and had not been the player the Steelers thought they were getting. He had struggled to become a reliable tackle. He was in the mix to start for the Steelers this season but when Max Iheanachor, this year's first-round pick by Pittsburgh, made his preseason debut Thursday then Jones became expendable.

For the Cowboys, it's one of the chances they often take on players who were graded highly coming out of college but didn't work out with their first team.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline: 4 players we want to see dealt to ideal landing spots include RBs Saquon Barkley and Jonathan Taylor
articles.summary: As rumors and buzz builds over deals in the NFL, Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab, Jay Busbee, Jori Epstein and Eric Edholm each weighed in on trades they want to...
articles.body:
The NFL trading season is heating up, and the Indianapolis Colts' fire sale is keeping the league warm .

The trade deadline is Nov. 10, but we've already had some notable deals go down this season involving the Dallas Cowboys (Joey Porter Jr.), Houston Texans (Marvin Harrison Jr.) and New York Giants (J.J. McCarthy).

As rumors and buzz builds over deals in the NFL, Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab , Jay Busbee , Jori Epstein and Eric Edholm each weighed in on trades they want to see in the coming days.

What trade do you want to see go down before the deadline?

Frank Schwab: The Colts are cooked, and they don't even have their 2027 first-round pick due to the Sauce Gardner trade. They probably wouldn't get a first-round pick back for Jonathan Taylor, but they could recoup some draft capital. And we saw Sunday night that the Seahawks have a tremendous defense and an offense that needs another star.

Seattle is still a Super Bowl contender, so why not, after dealing for Quenton Nelson on Tuesday afternoon , push some more chips in for Taylor, one of the NFL's best backs? It would add a massive boost to a team that still could be great this season and it would ensure Taylor isn't wasting another season of a great career on a horrendous Colts team. This is a win-win for everyone.

Jay Busbee: This is the time of year when the contenders start combing struggling teams' rosters like parents digging through their kids' Halloween candy. And although the Eagles and Chargers have a whole lot of Almond Joys and apple slices in there, there's still a full-size Snickers bar or two to be had if you look hard enough. Saquon Barkley, though coming off injury, makes for an enticing target for a team looking for instant ground offense.

One intriguing possibility: Minnesota, whose 2027 draft capital includes four picks in the first three rounds. How would Saquon look in purple? With that Super Bowl-caliber defense, pretty damn good.

Jori Epstein: A year ago, receiver Jauan Jennings averaged six targets per game for the San Francisco 49ers. In Minnesota, he's averaged 1.6. Sure, Jennings' value goes beyond his production with his blocking and physicality in the run game. His energy and bully mentality have historically balanced offenses with happy-go-lucky players. But the Vikings aren't getting the value in their one-year deal worth up to $8 million with $6.13 million guaranteed. So why not call the 49ers, who already reunited with defensive tackle DeForest Buckner on Tuesday ?

The Niners replaced Jennings and fellow former receivers with rookie De'Zhaun Stribling in the draft and veteran Mike Evans in free agency. Thanks to injuries, neither is currently available. Injuries perennially plague San Francisco; they're nearly a feature of the Kyle Shanahan grind rather than a bug. (I'm not suggesting anyone aspires to injuries, but some teams have a higher risk tolerance when working their teams in practice.)

So San Francisco needs insurance and should forget any hard feelings knowing Jennings can shoulder a segment of the load if needed. In return, Minnesota should recoup a Day 3 pick and some salary cap space to contribute toward an offensive complement that will help spark its 29th-ranked offense. No, 6-0 teams don't usually ship off players. But consider this shifting assets, Minnesota using the capital to grab a player the club will better utilize.

Eric Edholm: With DeForest Buckner headed to the 49ers , how about another fun reunion? Bears fans would be ecstatic for a Khalil Mack reprise. Chicago's pass rush could use a boost, and the Bears figure to be on the hunt for help.

I think a 2027 fourth- or fifth-round pick could get it done, considering Mack's age (35) and expiring contract.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ business ventures timeline: From Kansas City sports team investments in 2020 to Formula 1, restaurants and fitness brands
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is one of the biggest names in American football, but his business interests go far beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is one of the biggest names in American football, but his business interests go far beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs. Alongside his wife, Brittany Mahomes, he has invested in professional sports teams, restaurants, fitness technology, and other businesses. Their journey began with investments in Kansas City sports and later expanded to international motorsports and consumer brands. While Patrick has used his NFL success to build his investment portfolio, Brittany has played an important role in women’s soccer as a founding owner of the Kansas City Current.How did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes start their business journey?One of the couple’s earliest major business moves came in 2020, when Patrick joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Royals, a Major League Baseball team. His stake has been widely reported at around 1%, although the exact ownership details have not been fully disclosed publicly. The investment gave the NFL star a place in professional baseball ownership while he continued to build his career with the Chiefs.In 2021, Patrick expanded his sports investments by joining the ownership group of Sporting Kansas City, a Major League Soccer club. The move strengthened his connection with the city where he plays football and added another professional team to his portfolio.Brittany was building her own business interests around the same time. She became a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current, a National Women’s Soccer League team established in 2020. Her involvement made women’s soccer an important part of the couple’s business story, while Patrick later joined the ownership group.Their investments were not limited to sports. Patrick also entered the restaurant business through KMO Burgers, a franchise partnership connected to Whataburger. The arrangement helped bring the Texas-based burger chain to the Kansas City area, giving the football star a business interest in the fast-food industry.These early ventures established a pattern that continued in later years. Rather than depending only on football contracts and endorsement deals, Patrick and Brittany began investing in businesses that could operate and grow beyond his playing career.Which sports teams do Patrick and Brittany Mahomes own stakes in?Sports ownership has become one of the most visible parts of Patrick’s business portfolio. His investments include the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City, and the Kansas City Current, giving him connections to professional baseball and both men’s and women’s soccer.Patrick’s involvement with the Royals began in 2020, while he joined Sporting Kansas City’s ownership group in 2021. His investment in the Current followed in 2022, when he joined the club’s ownership group alongside Brittany and other investors. The Current announced his co-ownership in January 2023, describing him as the first active NFL player to hold an ownership stake in an NWSL club.The Current has also grown in reported financial value. Forbes valued the club at $75 million in 2024, $275 million in 2025, and $325 million in 2026. These figures show the rise in the team’s estimated value, although they do not reveal how much Patrick or Brittany personally made from their investments.Patrick also moved into international motorsports in October 2023, when he joined an investor group that acquired a 24% stake in the Alpine Formula 1 team. The group reportedly paid around $210 million for the combined stake, with other investors including NFL teammate Travis Kelce, actor Ryan Reynolds, golfer Rory McIlroy, and boxer Anthony Joshua.However, the $210 million investment was made by the group as a whole. Patrick’s individual contribution and ownership percentage have not been publicly disclosed, so it would be inaccurate to attribute the entire investment to him.What businesses and consumer brands have Patrick Mahomes invested in?Beyond sports teams, Patrick has developed interests in restaurants, fitness technology, and consumer products. His Whataburger franchise partnership is one example of his move into businesses that serve customers outside the sports world.Through KMO Burgers, Patrick became a franchise partner helping expand Whataburger in the Kansas City area. The investment gave him a connection to a well-known fast-food brand and added a local business venture to his portfolio.Patrick has also been linked to Throne Sport Coffee, a performance-focused coffee brand. Reports have described him as a lead investor and a major shareholder, although the precise size of his stake has not been publicly confirmed.Another notable investment is WHOOP, the wearable fitness technology company that makes devices used to track activity, recovery, and sleep. Patrick has been reported as an early investor in the company. WHOOP reached a reported valuation of $3.6 billion during a 2021 funding round, but that figure reflects the company’s valuation at that time, not the current value of Patrick’s investment.These ventures share a common theme. They connect Patrick’s public image as a professional athlete with products related to food, fitness, and performance. However, the amount he invested in each business and the returns he has received remain largely private.How have Patrick and Brittany Mahomes expanded their business ventures over time?The couple’s business timeline shows how their interests have grown across different industries.In 2020, Patrick joined the Kansas City Royals’ ownership group, while Brittany became a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current. These investments established their presence in professional sports ownership.In 2021, Patrick added Sporting Kansas City to his portfolio and expanded into the restaurant industry through his Whataburger franchise partnership. Around this period, he was also linked to investments in fitness technology, including WHOOP.In 2022, Patrick joined the Kansas City Current’s ownership group, building on Brittany’s existing role with the club. The team’s January 2023 announcement formally confirmed his co-ownership and highlighted the significance of an active NFL player investing in women’s professional soccer.Later in 2023, Patrick joined the investor group that acquired a minority stake in Alpine’s Formula 1 team. The move expanded his interests beyond Kansas City and into an international sport with a global audience.Their portfolio also extends beyond investments in operating businesses. Patrick founded 2PM Productions, a media production company, and established the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which supports initiatives benefiting children. These projects add media and philanthropy to his activities outside football.Brittany’s work with the Kansas City Current remains a key part of the couple’s business story. Her position as a founding owner gives her a direct role in women’s professional soccer, while Patrick’s investments span baseball, soccer, Formula 1, restaurants, and fitness technology.The couple’s individual ownership percentages and financial returns are not publicly available for most of these ventures. Still, their business history shows a clear move beyond football income and endorsements toward ownership interests across several industries. As Patrick continues his NFL career, these investments provide a foundation for business activities that can extend well beyond his time on the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2026, Reggie Bush launched a sports investment firm seeking $150 million to buy stakes in emerging leagues
articles.summary: Former NFL star Reggie Bush is taking his career in a new direction by investing in the future of sports.
articles.body: Former NFL star Reggie Bush is taking his career in a new direction by investing in the future of sports. In March 2026, Bush teamed up with investor Terrence C. Murphy Sr. to launch Synergy Sports Capital, a private-equity firm seeking $150 million for its first fund. The firm plans to invest in emerging sports leagues, teams, and related businesses instead of focusing mainly on established NFL and NBA franchises. With an investment in a professional soccer club already in place and a new golf venture in development, Bush and Murphy want to find business opportunities in sports that have room to grow. The move also gives Bush a chance to use his experience as a former player to understand what athletes and sports businesses need to succeed. By backing growing leagues and new ventures, Synergy Sports Capital hopes to find opportunities beyond traditional professional sports. The firm’s success will depend on choosing the right investments and helping these businesses build a stronger future.How the former NFL star and Terrence Murphy plan to invest in new sports competitionsSynergy Sports Capital plans to invest in sports teams and leagues while also exploring opportunities in real estate and businesses connected to the sports industry. Its first fund, Synergy Sports GP I, is seeking $150 million from potential investors, including wealthy individuals, family offices, private-equity firms, and professional athletes.According to Front Office Sports, Murphy said in March 2026 that the firm was speaking with potential investors and that some had made informal commitments. However, the report did not confirm that Synergy had raised the full amount.The firm has already made its first investment in Atlético Dallas, a soccer club founded in 2024 that competes in the USL Championship. It plans to explore further opportunities as it builds its portfolio.Murphy brings experience from his own investments, which include real estate and more than 100 companies. His sports-related investments include the United Pickleball Association and Third Coast Renegades Angling Club, a team in the Sport Fishing Championship league.Bush brings his experience as a former professional athlete and his understanding of the sports industry. Together, the two partners want to identify businesses that could benefit from investment and a stronger commercial strategy.Why their fund is targeting emerging leagues instead of established NFL and NBA franchisesBuying a stake in an established professional sports team has become popular among wealthy investors and athletes. However, these opportunities can require significant capital, and investors may have limited control over how a team operates.Synergy wants to take a different approach by focusing on emerging sports businesses where it may be able to acquire controlling stakes and play a more active role in their development.Murphy identified several competitions that reflect the firm’s areas of interest, including Unrivaled, the National Women’s Soccer League, Major League Pickleball, and TGL Golf. These organizations represent different parts of the sports industry, from women’s basketball and soccer to pickleball and technology-focused golf.The firm has not announced investments in all these leagues, so they remain potential areas of interest rather than confirmed deals.The strategy also involves looking beyond teams themselves. Synergy plans to consider sports-related real estate and businesses that support competitions, potentially giving it several ways to participate in the industry’s growth.However, emerging leagues can face challenges, including attracting fans, securing sponsors, and generating enough revenue to grow. Synergy will need to identify businesses with strong potential and determine how its investments can help them succeed.What is Synergy Sports Capital’s first investment, and which leagues could it target next?Atlético Dallas is currently Synergy’s first identified portfolio company. The club’s place in the USL Championship gives the firm an early presence in professional soccer as it looks for other investment opportunities.Murphy’s earlier investments in pickleball and competitive fishing also show his interest in sports outside the biggest professional leagues. These competitions can offer opportunities to build new audiences and attract sponsors, although their long-term success depends on their ability to grow.Synergy has not announced a complete list of future investments. Its next moves will depend on the opportunities available and how much money it raises through its inaugural fund.The firm is also interested in businesses connected to sports facilities, real estate, and league operations. This broader approach could allow it to invest in the infrastructure and services that help sports organizations operate, rather than relying only on team ownership.For now, Atlético Dallas remains its first identified investment, while other leagues and teams mentioned by Murphy represent possible opportunities rather than completed acquisitions.How Reggie Bush’s United Athletes Tour fits into the firm’s long-term business plansBush is also developing the United Athletes Tour, a golf venture designed for professional athletes who want to compete outside their main sports. After retiring from the NFL in 2017, Bush developed a strong interest in golf and noticed that many other athletes enjoyed the game but lacked a dedicated tour where they could compete for prize money and sponsorships.He told Front Office Sports that the tour was expected to hold its first event in June 2026 in San Diego, although he did not disclose the golf course at the time of the interview.Murphy said the project fits well with Synergy’s interest in emerging sports businesses. However, the report did not confirm the tour’s formal ownership structure within the firm.The venture could give athletes a new way to compete while creating opportunities for sponsors and other businesses. For Bush, it also provides a path to remain involved in sports while developing a business beyond his football career.Synergy Sports Capital is still in its early stages, and its progress will depend on fundraising and the investments it completes. Its $150 million target is a fundraising goal, not a confirmed amount already raised.With Atlético Dallas already in its portfolio and the United Athletes Tour taking shape, Bush and Murphy have begun putting their plans into action. Their next challenge will be to turn emerging sports opportunities into businesses that can attract audiences, generate revenue, and deliver long-term value for investors.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Justin Tucker’s addition raises questions about Kansas City Chiefs’ obsession with signing controversial players – why not Tyreek Hill then
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad after Harrison Butker struggled against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad after Harrison Butker struggled against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.This midseason signing reignites debate over the team’s steadfast and age-old willingness to sign controversial players. Justin Tucker served a 10-game suspension in 2025 following sexual misconduct allegations, which he has denied thoroughly.However, the recent move raises questions about Kansas City’s roster decisions and Andy Reid’s concerns over Harrison Butker’s performance.It also pushes a bigger question: why haven’t the Chiefs considered reuniting with another controversial former player, Tyreek Hill? Hill could strengthen Patrick Mahomes’ offense. But his legal proceedings with estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro continue to make headlines.Chiefs’ Justin Tucker signing raises Tyreek Hill questionsThe Kansas City Chiefs had their first 2026 NFL season loss in Week 7 vs. the Seattle Seahawks. The team scored 20-3. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker scored those 3 points.However, Butker couldn’t score two more field goals. How does the team address their collective loss? By adding Justin Tucker! As if that’s going to make it easy for Patrick Mahomes to move freely on the field. The Seahawks’ lethal defense completely limited the three-time Super Bowl champion.Anyhow, the recent signing of the former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker has refocused attention on Kansas City’s apparent obsession with signing controversial players.Justin Tucker missed time in 2025 because of sexual misconduct allegations. Much like Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson’s alleged charges. The misconduct allegedly happened during multiple massage sessions.Anyhow, Tucker served the 10-game suspension. And the Chiefs signed him to fill in for Harrison Butker. Butker didn’t just miss two of three field goals; he’s also a bit off his game. “He’s been one of the most consistent kickers in football,” Kansas City head coach Andy Reid said. “He’s off a bit. So gotta fix it.”Butker hasn’t appeared on the injury report, but the team probably wonders about his notable performance decline. Whatever the reason, this surely raises uncomfortable questions about the franchise’s approach to players facing serious off-gridiron allegations.And this surely takes us to the pressing 2026 offseason and even midseason question: why has Tyreek Hill not been signed by the Chiefs? Even when he’s one of the recent most controversial players.A Miami jury recently found Hill liable for two of 10 counts related to domestic violence and awarded his estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages in a highly charged civil trial.The Chiefs have shown an inclination to sign controversial players like Hill and many others in the past, as CBS Sports’ Jason La Canfora rightly pointed out in 2019.Clark Hunt’s past decisions invite scrutinyCBS Sports’ Jason La Canfora examined Clark Hunt-led Kansas City Chiefs’ past controversial player signings. Players like Kareem Hunt, Frank Clark, Jovan Belcher, and Tyreek Hill.Kareem Hunt assaulted a female in the 2018 NFL offseason, but he was allowed to practice and play. Frank Clark was arrested in 2014 for allegedly assaulting his then-girlfriend in an Ohio hotel.Jovan Belcher allegedly murdered his 22-year-old girlfriend Kasandra Perkins in the team’s parking lot in 2012. After allegedly murdering her, he shot himself in the head.Tyreek Hill’s 2019 leaked video showed his then-fiancee accusing him of abusing their three-year-old son. Hill was also sentenced for allegedly assaulting his pregnant girlfriend in college.These cases raise questions about how Kansas City’s leadership balances accountability, player conduct, and competitive ambitions. To top it off, another controversial player recently joined this list: Justin Tucker.Justin Tucker denies sexual misconduct allegationsJustin Tucker was allegedly accused by 16 massage therapists of exposing himself and other inappropriate behavior at Baltimore-area luxury spas. The incidents allegedly took place from 2012 to 2016. Two spas banned him from returning. However, he denied all allegations by posting a statement on social media, saying,“Throughout my career as a professional athlete, I’ve always sought to conduct myself with the utmost professionalism.I have never before been accused of misconduct of any kind, and I have never been accused of acting inappropriately in front of a massage therapist or during a massage therapy or during other bodywork.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New study estimates that nearly 75% of former NFL players had CTE at death
articles.summary: The population-based cross-sectional study, published Wednesday in the Journal of the American Medical Association, accounted for brain donation registry bia...
articles.body:
In August, a study published in the British Medical Journal estimated that at least 24.5% — roughly one in four — of former NFL players who died from 2016 to 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease linked to repeated hits to the head that involves a buildup of abnormal proteins that damage brain tissue.

On Wednesday, a new study — authored by many of the same researchers — came out with even more "sobering" numbers.

A study in JAMA Network Open estimated that approximately 74.5% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE, after adjusting for selection bias in brain donation.

Most of what we know about CTE in NFL players comes from autopsy-based studies on voluntarily donated brains, the study pointed out. Players suspected of having CTE are believed to be more likely to donate their brains than those who don't have it.

So, the JAMA study's objective was to estimate the selection-bias-adjusted prevalence of CTE in deceased NFL players.

This study consisted of 2,362 former NFL players, including 396 who had donated their brains. It ultimately determined that, while selection bias certainly inflates donor-based estimates — 93.5% of players studied who were brain donors with neuropathologic evaluation had CTE — the adjusted rate of CTE occurrence that was estimated remained strikingly high (74.5%).

Even the study's "conservative lower-bound analysis" estimated a 63.7% bias-adjusted population prevalence of CTE at death.

All of the NFL players included in the JAMA study played in at least one regular or postseason game.

The study used data from the Understanding Neurologic Injury and Traumatic Encephalopathy brain bank, plus National Death Index records on former NFL players.

"We first quantified the association of a derived clear cognitive symptoms variable with brain donation status and used this estimate to derive a selection ratio representing the relative probability of brain donation by CTE status," the study reads. "We then used this ratio to estimate the prevalence of CTE neuropathology among all deceased NFL players."

"We first quantified the association of a derived clear cognitive symptoms variable with brain donation status and used this estimate to derive a selection ratio representing the relative probability of brain donation by CTE status," the study reads.

"We then used this ratio to estimate the prevalence of CTE neuropathology among all deceased NFL players."

When estimating the "selection ratio," those conducting the JAMA study assumed that brain bank selection was primarily driven by family members of a former NFL player noticing cognitive symptoms.

From there, they used a National Death Index-derived binary dementia cause of death variable to estimate how much more likely people with a dementia-related cause of death were to become donors.

Although the study employed dementia cause of death as a proxy for CTE — due to CTE neuropathology's "large magnitude of association with dementia and cognitive symptoms" — the study acknowledged that many individuals with dementia or mild cognitive impairment will have cognitive symptoms but will die from a non-dementia-related cause.

To compensate for the anticipated measurement error associated with that proxy variable, those conducting the study used population-level estimates of mild cognitive impairment and dementia in former NFL players older than 50 years that were reported in a 2022 study in order to expand their definition of "clear cognitive symptoms."

Notably, the JAMA study also estimated that the bias-adjusted population prevalence of all-cause dementia history during life among the former NFL players studied was 27.2%.

CTE is a condition that, at the moment, can be diagnosed only after death. Following the publication of the aforementioned BMJ study in August, the NFL issued a statement.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing," an NFL spokesperson said at the time in a statement obtained by Yahoo Sports, in part. "We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

Although CTE risk in all levels of football appears difficult to substantially mitigate, researchers believe treating symptoms of repetitive brain injury during players' lives, particularly during the years between a player's retirement and death, could limit CTE's long-term impact.

Upgrading that health care could complement the league's safety initiatives, which have included helmet regulations, stricter concussion protocols and the dramatic transformation of the NFL kickoff.

articles.title: Colts' fire sale can help with impending QB problem, but it won't be easy
articles.summary: The Colts have a lot to figure out in the coming months, and their quarterback problem might be the most concerning element.
articles.body:
What follows is anyone's guess, but the road eventually must lead to where Ballard struggled to: closer to quarterback salvation.

The franchise has a lot to figure out in the next six or so months, and only limited resources with which to do so.

Head coach Shane Steichen, 2-5 this season and 27-31 overall, could be fighting for his job — and now with less talent at hand.

Interim GM Ed Dodds, who replaced the fired Ballard, has a very short window to prove he's the man for the full-time job.

And the quarterback problem isn't going away.

That's in addition to plugging the various roster holes, which have only increased this week. Doing so without a first-round draft choice in 2027 only ups the degree of difficulty. The Colts could hit grand slams with their head coach and GM decisions, and they'd still find themselves in a tough QB spot next spring.

Let's dive into what the Colts have now, their limitations for upgrading the position from Daniel Jones and what the most realistic solutions might be.

Jones is the starter now, as Steichen has stuck with him despite his 2026 struggles, but the eight-year veteran does not appear to be a long-term solution in Indianapolis. There was hope after his strong play last season, but Jones has been turning the ball over at an alarming rate coming off an Achilles injury that ended last season.

If he's still on the roster next March, Jones would be owed another $10 million guaranteed and a $4 million roster bonus. Keeping him, especially with that kicker, just doesn't equate right now.

The Colts drafted Anthony Richardson Sr. fourth overall in 2023, but he's taken about only a dozen regular-season snaps since his final start in the 2024 campaign. The way the Colts have acted the past few seasons, they've chalked him up to a sunk cost and merely stashing him in case of emergency. Richardson is a free agent next spring, and it would be a surprise to see him back as well.

Riley Leonard is the only realistic option on the roster now to stick around. He had a few intriguing moments last season, including the Week 18 start at Houston, that kept him with the Colts. If Jones keeps stumbling, they could turn to him this season down the stretch.

But how solid an asset is Leonard? The Colts likely need more game film to decide, but there's a ceiling right now to the former sixth-round pick's potential. Keep in mind that the Colts bypassed Leonard at first last season for signing Philip Rivers, who was four years removed from his last game, before giving him a meaningless-game shot.

In short, there's not a whole lot to count on. Expect a largely — and perhaps entirely — new QB room in 2027.

Most likely route to finding a 2027 starter

Free agency is a very limited route to finding a starting quarterback because few teams will allow high-quality options to walk unimpeded in free agency. Sam Darnold situations occur every few years, but they're not terribly common events all told.

Point being: The Colts have to understand that any QB options they might consider as unrestricted free agents almost always come with warts.

Deshaun Watson is a perfect example. Even if he plays acceptably well for the remainder of the season with the Cleveland Browns, signing him as a free agent — yes, he finally hits the market again — comes with a ton of baggage and likely wouldn't inspire the fan base.

Justin Fields isn't on the Darnold spectrum yet, even if he's a highly-paid backup with 53 career starts. The same probably applies to the likes of Davis Mills and Jarrett Stidham.

The one possibly intriguing option among the free agents to-be is likely the 49ers' Mac Jones. He's started 53 games, has marinated in the 49ers' system for a few years and stepped in readily for an injured Brock Purdy a year ago. The Jones likelihood only increases if the Colts consider any 49ers assistants (Klay Kubiak, perhaps?) as a head-coaching candidate.

Otherwise, the Colts would be shopping on some familiar streets with some of the veteran options who'll be available, including Jacoby Brissett, Kirk Cousins and Marcus Mariota. Those aren't bad options if the Colts can pair them with a young QB and sell the veteran on a bridge-QB role for 2027.

Can the Colts find QB help in the 2027 draft?

This leads us to the other elephant in the room. The 2027 NFL Draft, once pegged as a possibly generational class at quarterback, now looks tepid in some respects. There are some quality prospects in the 2027 mix, but the class as a whole has not taken off as hoped.

The Colts lack their 2027 first-round pick from the Sauce Gardner trade, and even after the Nelson and Buckner trades, they currently have only one guaranteed top-64 selection. The extra mid-round selections could allow a trade-up situation from high in Round 2, assuming the Colts finish with a losing record, but it still would be a heavier lift to get into the first round.

For years, the late first- to early second-round range was a wasteland for quarterbacks, but in the past decade it has produced Lamar Jackson, Jordan Love, Tyler Shough and Jaxson Dart. It has also given us Will Levis and Drew Lock. But on the whole, you'd say any draft range that theoretically produces a better-than-50% ROI has to be considered fertile grounds.

Even if next year's class isn't what we had hoped, there still could be options who project in a similar range.

One is Oregon's Dante Moore. He might have been the No. 2 overall draft pick had he come out a year ago, but Moore's slower start this season and a season-ending concussion have his draft stock hanging in the void. It's possible he could slide and be within range of where the Colts end up picking.

Miami's Darian Mensah might be trending toward a first-round landing spot, but that's not guaranteed yet. USC's Jayden Maiava, who is out of eligibility after this season, will be in the upcoming class, and he's played well this season; his range has yet to crystallize, but he's another who might not be far out of reach.

There could be other candidates, including Notre Dame's C.J. Carr, Missouri's Austin Simmons and Ohio State's Julian Sayin, but all of them will have options to return to school. The wild card might be South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, but as a very toolsy but flawed prospect, Sellers might hit a little too optically close to the Richardson mark to be the preferred choice.

The answer to our original question is probably a soft "yes." The Colts can find someone with some potential upside, but it might require a mix of luck and aggression come draft time. The outlook at this point is far from dim, but it's also not wholly inspiring.

Best guess right now is that the Colts — whoever is running them in three months as GM — will opt to pair a veteran free agent with Leonard and a draft prospect who ranks somewhere between QB3 and QB6 on most consensus boards.

Is it an exciting plan? Maybe not, but given the Colts' situation and the deep rebuild they're facing, it probably could be worse.

articles.title: NFL Fantasy Football Week 8 2026 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Tight End
articles.summary: A tight end can spend most of an afternoon focused on blocking, and then suddenly catch a touchdown in the fourth quarter, finishing the game ahead of a play...
articles.body:
A tight end can spend most of an afternoon focused on blocking, and then suddenly catch a touchdown in the fourth quarter, finishing the game ahead of a player who was heavily involved in the passing game from the start. Fantasy managers have learned to manage this kind of frustration. However, Week 8 brings several situations where the underlying opportunities provide more insight than the final score from the previous week.

In New England, there is a reliable connection forming between Drake Maye and Hunter Henry . Meanwhile, Minnesota is preparing for a divisional matchup against a defense that has struggled significantly against tight ends. Additionally, two young, productive players are facing opponents that may make their typical routes less effective.

Here are three tight ends worth starting and three who may disappoint in Week 8.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Start 'Em: Patriots' Hunter Henry at Dolphins

Hunter Henry has emerged as one of the most valuable players in New England's passing offense, and his recent performances suggest that fantasy managers should stop viewing him as just an emergency replacement. In the game against Chicago last Thursday, Henry caught all seven of his targets for 71 yards, setting seasonal highs in both receptions and receiving yards. He has now recorded between 44 and 71 yards in four consecutive games, which is encouraging for a position where even respectable starters often struggle to reach 40 yards.

The Patriots have given Henry a significant role in their passing game, especially when Drake Maye needs a reliable receiver in the middle of the field. His ability to recognize coverage and find openings against linebackers makes him an asset during drives that require multiple successful completions.

Miami has faced significant challenges defending tight ends this season. Over six games, the Dolphins have allowed 44 receptions, 448 yards, and six touchdowns to tight ends.

These statistics present a strong opportunity for Henry, whose involvement already provides a solid foundation in PPR (points per reception) formats. He has also shown he can contribute near the goal line, scoring in consecutive games earlier this month.

Start 'Em: Vikings' T.J. Hockenson at Lions

T.J. Hockenson is set to return to Detroit in a matchup that could enable him to achieve his most productive fantasy performance since early October. The veteran tight end has had an interrupted season, including a concussion that caused him to miss some games. He made his comeback in Week 7 against Indianapolis, catching four passes for 35 yards and a touchdown, which is an encouraging sign that he remains a key contributor to Minnesota's offense.

His previous standout performance was against Miami, where he caught 13 passes for 119 yards. This game demonstrated how much Kyler Murray can rely on him as a dependable receiving option when the Vikings need it most. Detroit's defense has shown particular vulnerability to tight ends, allowing 10 touchdowns to the position over the first six games. Opponents have consistently succeeded in attacking the middle of the field and creating favorable matchups near the end zone.

While Minnesota has occasionally struggled with consistent passing production, the Lions have an offense that can force a more aggressive game plan. If Detroit takes an early lead, Murray may need to depend more heavily on short and intermediate throws to keep drives alive.

Start 'Em: Jets' Mason Taylor vs. Raiders

Mason Taylor's performance against Miami should catch the eyes of fantasy managers looking for a potential breakout player. However, the most encouraging aspect of his game goes beyond just the two touchdowns he scored.

The second-year tight end caught five of six targets for 62 yards , scoring twice and successfully converting a two-point attempt during New York's narrow 28-25 loss. Taylor's ability to sustain drives was evident as he produced four first downs, stepping up in critical moments that required a reliable receiving option. His involvement in the offense has increased over the past three games. After recording three receptions against Cleveland and four against New England, he delivered his best performance of the season against Miami.

While the Jets have other receiving options, including Garrett Wilson and emerging rookie Omar Cooper Jr., Geno Smith has shown a growing trust in Taylor, particularly when targeting the middle of the field.

Sit 'Em: Bears' Colston Loveland at Seahawks

Colston Loveland has provided a much-needed receiving presence for Chicago's offense, especially in light of Cole Kmet's injury. His recent performances have been encouraging enough that fantasy managers may be reluctant to bench him. However, the upcoming matchup against Seattle raises some important considerations.

The Seahawks have proven to be one of the NFL's most effective defenses against tight ends, consistently limiting their receiving opportunities and preventing players from turning short completions into significant gains. For instance, in Week 7, Kansas City's Travis Kelce managed only four receptions for 44 yards, despite being targeted eight times. Loveland has shown increasing involvement in Chicago's passing game, and his growing chemistry with quarterback Caleb Williams offers genuine reasons for optimism beyond this particular matchup.

Yet, Seattle's defensive structure might force Williams to look for alternatives, as the Seahawks excel at denying receivers open space between the linebackers and safeties.

Sam LaPorta is one of Detroit's most talented receiving options, but facing Minnesota presents a tough challenge for any tight end. LaPorta has seen a boost in his production lately, thanks to an offense that creates favorable matchups through its talented receiving corps. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs draw significant defensive attention, which often helps LaPorta find opportunities against opponents who struggle to cover all the threats.

However, Brian Flores' defense poses a different challenge. The Vikings have not allowed a receiving touchdown to a tight end in their first six games and have consistently limited production at that position. They employ changing coverage responsibilities and aggressive defensive schemes to disrupt passing plays, making it hard for quarterbacks to identify reliable options before the snap.

Jared Goff is still capable of connecting with LaPorta when the matchup permits, and Detroit's offensive talent ensures that no single receiver becomes completely unplayable.

However, fantasy managers should temper their expectations.

Sit 'Em: Cowboys' Jake Ferguson vs. Cardinals

Jake Ferguson's fantasy value has become increasingly difficult to predict as the Dallas Cowboys continue to find production through other offensive contributors. The Cowboys scored 38 points against Philadelphia on Monday, showcasing how effective their offense can be without heavily relying on Ferguson. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens as dangerous receiving options for Dak Prescott, the competition at tight end has intensified, particularly with Brevyn Spann-Ford earning more opportunities. This distribution creates uncertainty for fantasy managers who seek consistent receptions from their starting tight end.

While Arizona's defensive struggles could lead to a productive afternoon for Dallas, a favorable matchup does not guarantee substantial involvement for Ferguson. If the Cowboys establish an early lead through explosive passing plays and a strong rushing attack, Ferguson may spend much of the game blocking instead of accumulating targets.

The top tight end opportunities in Week 8 are for players whose offenses have clearly defined receiving roles. Hunter Henry has developed a reliable connection with quarterback Maye, while T.J. Hockenson has a particularly advantageous matchup against his former team.

Fantasy managers should carefully evaluate how each player is utilized before allowing last week's touchdowns to dictate this week's lineup decisions.

articles.title: Fox Sports star hopes Justin Tucker ‘never plays a snap for the Chiefs’
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs ruffled feathers on Wednesday by signing former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. The 37-year-old, who played for...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs ruffled feathers on Wednesday by signing former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. The 37-year-old, who played for the Baltimore Ravens from 2012-2024, was once considered arguably the best NFL kicker in league history, but his reputation never recovered after The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct.

Per T he Baltimore Banner, the alleged misconduct took place between 2012 and 2016, although Tucker has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

"I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists."

Even with his denials, Kansas City signing him to the practice squad was a widely panned move across the NFL world, and Fox Sports analyst made it clear that he doesn't want him to see the field for his favorite team this year.

"Going on the record that I hope Justin Tucker never plays a snap for the Chiefs," Wright wrote on X. "For those wondering, I feel the same way about Tyreek. If you want to hear my deeper thoughts about a potential Tyreek signing (many apply to Tucker), I did them 2 weeks ago, and here they are."

In his media session on Wednesday, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that Tucker has already served his punishment from the NFL ( a 10-game suspension) and that he'd be leaving things there.

"I'm not going to get into all of that," Reid said. "To bring him in here, I did some homework. He's here, and he's on the practice squad, so we roll with it."

The Chiefs have not announced if Tucker will be on the active roster on Sunday against the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Vikings LB Blake Cashman Named Week 7 NFC Defensive POTW
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings LB Blake Cashman has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7. He was announced as the selection after a dominant perform...
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings LB Blake Cashman has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7 . He was announced as the selection after a dominant performance in the Minnesota Vikings' 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts .

The middle linebacker finished with 12 tackles (eight solo), including two for loss, two sacks, three quarterback hits, and four passes defensed. The sack total and pass breakups were both career highs. He was all over the field in a game where the Vikings' defense limited the Colts after an early touchdown and helped preserve the team's undefeated record. Ultimately, if you were watching the game, Blake Cashman was playing out of his mind.

The numbers were great, but it has been something we are starting to just expect from Blake. Cashman became the first player since Chicago's Alex Brown in 2005 to record at least two sacks and four passes defensed in the same game. He was also the first since sacks became an official statistic in 1982 to post 12 tackles, two sacks, and four passes defensed in a single outing. Adding to the personal achievements, it was his 20th career game with double-digit tackles and the 16th since he joined the Vikings. He has now recorded at least seven tackles in 17 straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest by a Viking since at least 1987.

Blake is from Eden Prairie, Minnesota. Played at the University of Minnesota as a Golden Gopher as a walk-on. He is now playing professionally as a Minnesota Viking. You can't have enough of a hometown dream scenario than that. As a fan, you have been able to cheer for him throughout his career. Makes him one of the most popular players on the team by far. But Blake is in a contract year, and with the Vikings not signing him to a contract before the season, the price will only continue to go up with his play and achievements.

This is Cashman's second career Defensive Player of the Week honor. He previously won the AFC version in 2023 while with the Houston Texans . Since being with the Vikings, he has been a fantastic leader on defense. He is the green-dot communicator in Brian Flores' defense and has been one of the more consistent playmakers on a defense ranked number one in the NFL in numerous categories.

The award continues a strong run of weekly recognition for the Vikings on defense and special teams this year. Isaiah Rodgers won NFC Special Teams Player of the Week in Week 2 after blocking a field goal against the Bears. Myles Price earned the same honor in Week 3 for an 86-yard punt return touchdown against Tampa Bay. Will Reichard took it in Week 4 after going 5-for-5 on field goals and scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points against Miami. Byron Murphy Jr. was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week in Week 5 after recording two interceptions in New Orleans . Cashman's selection makes it five weekly awards for the team in a five-game stretch.

The Vikings head to Detroit next with the league's only remaining undefeated record. Cashman's performance against the Colts was the clearest individual example yet of why the defense has been so dominant. Leaders and performers like Cashman are executing this Brian Flores defense expertly and will look to keep it going against their NFC Rival in, the Lions , in Week 8.
